Marissa / Dev —

Natalie sent over their network diagram and prefers isolated peered VPCs; tentative install windows Jan 25 or Feb 1. Legal will review SOW. 

Please own the following: 
- Marissa: coordinate the customer-facing kickoff, confirm final list of participants, and track DocuSign SOW.
- Dev: perform a technical review of their diagram, propose peering model (VPC peering or PrivateLink), and list required firewall rules, subnets, and port ranges.

Important constraints from Natalie: avoid transitive routing through prod VPCs; prefer non-intrusive route table changes and minimal blast radius. Also request for HSM-backed KMS keys for key material (we support KMS integration).

I’ve attached the preflight checklist; please annotate and send back to Natalie with a proposed maintenance window from our side.

- Rishi

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 9 Jan 2027 14:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Internal: Elysian Health - network review + owners

Rishi / Marissa —

Quick technical notes after reviewing elysian_network_diagram_v2.png: 
- Recommend VPC peering between Redwood-managed VPC (10.20.0.0/16) and Elysian's isolated service VPC (10.120.0.0/16). Peering avoids NAT complexity and keeps traffic internal.
- Route propagation: Customer must add explicit routes in the service VPC route table pointed at the peering attachment. Ensure no propagation into prod VPC route tables.
- Required ports: TCP 443 (API), TCP 10250 (agent management), ICMP for basic MTU/path MTU discovery. If using PrivateLink, we need TLS ALPN support on their side.
- BGP: Not required for our setup; static routes are fine.
- MTU and jumbo frames: confirm their switch configuration; we recommend 1500.
- KMS/HSM: we will accept customer-managed KMS keys; provide key ARN and grant Encrypt/Decrypt permissions to redwood-service-role.

I’ve attached our internal peering guide snippet for their network team to review. Also: during install we'll request a bastion (temporary) for secure package delivery and validation — ephemeral creds only.

Proposed implementation window from Redwood: Jan 26 02:00-06:00 UTC (which maps to Jan 25 morning ET). If they confirm Jan 25 ET, we can do Jan 26 UTC.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Implementation Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_vpc_peering_guide.pdf (PDF)]

3) Redwood deliverables:

Proposed install: Jan 26 02:00-06:00 UTC (customer-visible window Jan 25 morning ET). Please confirm whether Jan 25 morning ET works for network and security to be available for the smoke tests. If Jan 25 works, I’ll lock in the window and send the DocuSign link to Natalie.

Best,
